notes: Historical financials (revenue, operating income as EBIT, D&A, capex, and balance sheet inputs for NWC) are extracted from Pool Corporation Form 10-Ks for FY ended Dec 31, 2023-2025. EBIT is defined as 'Operating income' from the Consolidated Statements of Income. D&A is defined as 'Depreciation' + 'Amortization' from the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows. Capex is defined as 'Purchases of property and equipment, net of sale proceeds' from the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows. ([stocklight.com](https://stocklight.com/stocks/us/nasdaq-pool/pool-corporation/annual-reports/nasdaq-pool-2025-10K-25680506.pdf))

NWC construction for the historical 'nwc' line item is: (Total current assets − cash and cash equivalents) − (Total current liabilities − short-term borrowings and current portion of long-term debt), using year-end balance sheet values (leases excluded). ([stocklight.com](https://stocklight.com/stocks/us/nasdaq-pool/pool-corporation/annual-reports/nasdaq-pool-2024-10K-24685934.pdf))

Tax rate uses FY2023 effective rate as a proxy (income tax provision / income before income taxes and equity in earnings). ([stocklight.com](https://stocklight.com/stocks/us/nasdaq-pool/pool-corporation/annual-reports/nasdaq-pool-2024-10K-24685934.pdf))

catalysts: Improvement in discretionary volumes tied to pool construction/remodel activity (weather normalization and housing turnover).
Evidence of sustained margin progress from mix, pricing discipline, and operating expense control.
Continued shareholder returns if operating cash flow remains resilient through the seasonal demand cycle.
company_overview: World’s largest wholesale distributor of swimming pool supplies, equipment and related leisure products; also a leading distributor of irrigation and landscape maintenance products. ([stocklight.com](https://stocklight.com/stocks/us/nasdaq-pool/pool-corporation/annual-reports/nasdaq-pool-2026-10K-26683874.pdf))

Operates 456 sales centers across North America, Europe, and Australia to serve a diversified customer base (pool builders, pool service companies, retail stores, commercial pool operators, and landscape contractors). ([stocklight.com](https://stocklight.com/stocks/us/nasdaq-pool/pool-corporation/annual-reports/nasdaq-pool-2026-10K-26683874.pdf))

Product demand mix is weighted to recurring maintenance/minor repair (approximately 64% of sales), supporting cash flow resilience through housing cycles. ([stocklight.com](https://stocklight.com/stocks/us/nasdaq-pool/pool-corporation/annual-reports/nasdaq-pool-2026-10K-26683874.pdf))

Remaining exposure includes remodeling/renovations/upgrades (approximately 22% of sales) and new pool construction (approximately 14% of sales). ([stocklight.com](https://stocklight.com/stocks/us/nasdaq-pool/pool-corporation/annual-reports/nasdaq-pool-2026-10K-26683874.pdf))
current_context: Latest disclosed outlook (Q4/FY 2025 results release): 2026 diluted EPS guidance of $10.85–$11.15 (excluding ASU 2016-09 tax benefits), reflecting modest sales growth and improved earnings. ([ir.poolcorp.com](https://ir.poolcorp.com/pool-corporation-reports-year-end-and-fourth-quarter-2025-results-provides-2026-earnings-guidance/?utm_source=openai))

Business positioning centers on steady non-discretionary demand with discretionary items (remodel/new construction) driving variability around the mean. ([stocklight.com](https://stocklight.com/stocks/us/nasdaq-pool/pool-corporation/annual-reports/nasdaq-pool-2026-10K-26683874.pdf))
investment_highlights: Recurring maintenance/minor repair demand (majority of sales) anchors revenue assumptions to low-single-digit growth rather than assuming a housing boom. ([stocklight.com](https://stocklight.com/stocks/us/nasdaq-pool/pool-corporation/annual-reports/nasdaq-pool-2026-10K-26683874.pdf))
Base-case EBIT margin gradually normalizes from FY2025 levels toward a mid-cycle target (reflecting operating leverage without assuming a rapid margin snap-back).

Capital intensity remains modest historically (capex ~1%–1.1% of sales), and the model holds capex_pct_sales near that level. ([stocklight.com](https://stocklight.com/stocks/us/nasdaq-pool/pool-corporation/annual-reports/nasdaq-pool-2024-10K-24685934.pdf))

Working-capital intensity is modeled using an NWC-to-sales ratio around the historical center of mass, capturing the distributor’s inventory/accounts payable dynamics. ([stocklight.com](https://stocklight.com/stocks/us/nasdaq-pool/pool-corporation/annual-reports/nasdaq-pool-2024-10K-24685934.pdf))
Terminal value is driven by an exit EBITDA multiple consistent with a mature distributor/aftermarket cash generator, with bull/bear sensitivities capturing valuation compression/expansion.
key_risks: Downward pressure on discretionary remodeling/new construction if housing activity weakens further than expected.
Weather shocks and seasonal working-capital swings that can amplify quarter-to-quarter results and free cash flow.
Input cost inflation or pricing/competitive pressure that prevents margin normalization.
